item.title: Astros reportedly pick next manager as announcement nears
item.description: General Manager Randy Flores and owner Jim Crane of the Houston Astros answer questions from the media at an introductory press conference after Flores signed a contract with the Houston Astros at Daikin Park on November 02, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Houston Astros/Getty Images) After parting ways with Joe Espada, the Houston Astros appear to be close to naming their next manager, with an announcement potentially coming as soon as today. Multiple reports indicate the team has settled on a candidate to take over the dugout, though it has not officially announced the decision. According to KHOU Baseball analyst Jeremy Booth, the newly hired general manager Randy Flores has made his decision on the team's next manager. The shortlist of candidates, which includes former St. Louis Cardinals slugger Albert Pujols, former Astros catcher Brad Ausmus, and former Astros third baseman Morgan Ensberg, will be notified shortly after the contracts are officially signed. Hearing the #Astros have selected their next manager and should notify candidates shortly after they dot I's and cross T's. I'd imagine they announce after that's done rather than have a repeat of the previous situation. As always with this organization, things can change at any moment. But, with Randy in charge you can already feel the change with how things are led. #Astros @KHOU - Jeremy Booth (@_JeremyBooth) November 10, 2026 Houston sports radio host Lance Zierlein said on X that John Granato, host of The Bench on ESPN 97.5 Houston, announced on his morning show that sources have confirmed former Astros catcher Brad Ausmus has been selected as the team's next manager. On our show just now, @johngranato just announced that sources have confided that Brad Ausmus will be the Astros next manager. https://t.co/PVYfEMtjA3 - Lance Zierlein (@LanceZierlein) November 11, 2026 At Tuesday's General Managers Meeting in Las Vegas, Flores said he and the organization hope to make a decision soon, indicating an announcement could come by the end of the week. "My hope is I get back to Houston at the end of this week, hopefully finalize our manager decision and spend the next week in bunker-down mode filling out our Major League staff and the order of operations of tackling our team and roster construction," Flores said. The Astros are reportedly close to naming a new manager. (Photo by Michaela Schumacher/MLB Photos via Getty Images) (Michaela Schumacher/MLB Photos via Getty Images) Astros owner Jim Crane , senior advisor to ownership and baseball operations Jeff Bagwell, and the Astros' two assistant general managers Charles Cook and Gavin Dickey all participated in the interview process, according to Flores. Pujols reportedly interviewed last Thursday in Houston, and Ausmus had previously interviewed for the vacant general manager position. Texas Rangers bench coach Luis Urueta has also interviewed for the job. Flores, a former relief pitcher for the Cardinals, was a teammate of Pujols from 2004 to 2008.

item.title: New Report Offers NY Mets Second Chance at the Mason Miller Trade They Let Get Away Last Year
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A new report opens the door, just a crack, for the New York Mets to again pursue a trade for superstar closer Mason Miller this offseason. With a lockout looming on Dec. 1, there is a belief around MLB that teams will look to be more aggressive than normal at this week’s general manager meetings to get deals done before payroll guidelines change in the next collective bargaining agreement. You can certainly count the Mets among that group. Last year, Mets decision-makers reportedly spoke with their counterparts from the San Diego Padres about a variety of trade ideas. The rumors suggested closer Mason Miller was a part of those discussions. Obviously, a deal never happened, and the New York front office surely regrets it after the 28-year-old had an outstanding 2026 season. Posting a 1.67 ERA, 38 saves, and 129 strikeouts to 26 walks. Well, the opportunity to acquire him may be possible this month. In a new report, USA Today’s Bob Nightengale floated the idea that Padres GM AJ Preller might consider moving the All-Star this offseason to improve the roster. While the idea would seem ludicrous, the MLB insider notes San Diego has little wiggle room to make moves because Manny Machado, Fernando Tatis, and Xander Bogaerts are owed $721 million and “they each have no-trade clauses.” It means if the Padres want to add to the roster or even their farm system, they might need to move some of the few valuable trade chips they have. What could a Mason Miller trade cost the New York Mets this time around? Sep 30, 2026; San Diego, California, USA; San Diego Padres pitcher Mason Miller (22) reacts after the game against the Chicago Cubs during game two of the Wildcard round for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Petco Park. Mandatory Credit: Denis Poroy-Imagn Images Miller would be a huge addition for the Mets and bring further security to their bullpen after they traded a handful of relievers before last season’s deadline. Furthermore, there have been rumblings off and on in recent years that the two-time All-Star could be a candidate to make the transition to being a starter. New York had success doing that with Clay Holmes two years ago. If they feel Miller can also make the move, it would give them an interesting option for their rotation who is still under arbitration control for three more years . But the Padres won’t give him away. So what could a trade cost the Mets? Nightengale notes that the Padres will be searching for affordable pitching this offseason because they could lose Michael King, Nick Pivetta, and Adrian Morejon in free agency this offseason. New York could offer young arms with upside like Zach Thornton and Jonah Tong in a potential deal. Furthermore, top-10 pitching prospects Jonathan Santucci and Jack Wenninger might interest San Diego as part of a trade package. If the Padres are looking for changes in left field or at DH, Mark Vientos and Brett Baty could be a part of a trade because they do offer versatility

item.title: Hamilton and Leclerc Clashed Again in Brazil? Here’s What They Actually Said
item.description: Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc played down a brief on-track battle in the F1 São Paulo GP, amid recent tensions between the Ferrari teammates. It was only for a brief moment, but both Ferrari ’s Hamilton and Leclerc crossed paths at the F1 São Paulo GP at Interlagos when the Brit started from the back, and the Monegasque was in the midfield. Hamilton made a storming start from the back of the grid and passed Leclerc on Lap 1. However, his tire started to degrade, which allowed Leclerc to get on his tail soon. The Monegasque caught up with him and passed him with ease. Hamilton, Leclerc on the São Paulo GP Battle “I don’t really remember it, but yeah, I think there was a moment where we were close with one another, and yep, it was good,” said Hamilton to the media after the F1 São Paulo GP. At the same time, Leclerc responded: “Yeah, Lewis was much faster than me, so at that time there was no point for me to fight.” Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc. Image Credit: Scuderia Ferrari Hamilton Says Things Are Sorted and They Move On In terms of results, the Grand Prix wasn’t as good for Ferrari, with Leclerc ending up eighth and Hamilton ninth. The Monegasque finished seventh, but a post-race penalty after contact with Liam Lawson dropped him to eighth. It followed a weekend of talks and discussions involving the two F1 drivers and also team boss Frederic Vasseur . As things stand, things seem sorted for now. Hamilton talked about a good discussion on Saturday, and that they squashed things down after a healthy one-on-one discussion. “Yes, everything’s good,” said Hamilton. “Fred brought us together, and Fred was great in the meeting, and then he let me and Charles just give our points, and we both had a really good open discussion, and it’s all good, and we just move on.”

item.title: Memorial Park in Houston opens splash pad for LPGA major winner's leap
item.description: Nelly Korda won the 2026 Chevron Championship and jumped into a makeshift pool on the side of the 18th green at Memorial Park in Houston. The next winner of the LPGA major will get to jump into an actual pond. Golf course architect Tom Doak returned to help redo the 18th hole by adding a pond down the right side of the green. It enables the winner to maintain the tradition of the major — which was played for some 50 years at Rancho Mirage in California — by jumping into the water. It’s not Poppie’s Pond , but it will have to do. The 18th hole opened for public play over the weekend. Memorial Park also hosts the Houston Open held two weeks before the Masters. Gary Woodland won that event in April in dramatic fashion, capturing his first title in since his 2019 U.S. Open win at Pebble Beach. That triumph came weeks after Woodland revealed he was battling symptoms from PTSD after having a lesion removed from his brain. item.title: O'Sullivan loses 4-0 to Murphy at Champion of Champions
item.description: O'Sullivan won the last of his seven world titles in 2022 [Getty Images] Seven-time world champion Ronnie O'Sullivan suffered a 4-0 defeat by Shaun Murphy at the Champion of Champions tournament in Leicester. O'Sullivan, who has been struggling for form, was playing for the first time since losing to Ka Wai Cheung at the Northern Ireland Open last month. The 50-year-old found himself 2-0 down against Murphy, who knocked in a 68 in the second frame. Murphy made a 41 break to take the next frame before taking a tense fourth frame 61-42 to secure victory and a spot in the last eight. He will play the winner of the other Group Three match between world champion Wu Yize and Chang Bingyu.

item.description: Why Paul George Flipped Off a 76ers Fan in Return to Philadelphia originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Tuesday's battle between the Celtics and 76ers was all about Jaylen Brown's first face-off with Jayson Tatum, but Paul George stole the show in more ways than one. George looked like the best player on the floor, scoring 36 points on 14-of-22 shooting in a comfortable 123-101 win, picking up his Celtics teammates and giving his former fans in Philadelphia a show. The nine-time All-Star also gave 76ers fans something else: a middle finger. Here's how George explained flipping off 76ers fans after he faced his former team on Tuesday night. Looks like Paul George may have also flipped out a fan (or someone) after that three https://t.co/LecXldKldE — Noa Dalzell 🏀 (@NoaDalzell) November 11, 2026 While no one would be surprised to hear 76ers were taunting George in his first game against his former team, the Celtics star was pretty specific about what exactly happened. "There was a fan being an a—hole," George told CelticsBlog's Noa Dalzell. "Looked me in my eyes, dropped the ball on the ground as if I'm a dog to go fetch or go get it instead of passing the ball to me as a normal fan would do, and so yeah, so then I rolled him a middle finger in return." Asked Paul George what happened here: “There was a fan being an asshole. Dropped the ball on the ground as if like I'm a dog to go fetch or go get it instead of passing the ball to me like a normal fan would do, and so yeah, so then I rolled him a middle finger in return.” https://t.co/W1feMuJzBe — Noa Dalzell 🏀 (@NoaDalzell) November 11, 2026 George might not have had a truly adversarial relationship with 76ers fans during his two seasons in Philadelphia, but even he admitted he didn't play his best with the organization due to his health. "Quite frankly I wasn't healthy to take on the workload that I feel I'm at my best at," George said on Tuesday about his time with the 76ers. Philadelphia fans are undoubtedly happy with their current situation after a hot start to the season, but George got the better of Brown and the Sixers in their first of what could be many meetings to come. The question is, can they do it again? Given both the Jags and Colts were playing such good football, winning the division was out of the question. The Jags play the Titans two out of the next three games and also have Dallas (4-5), Washington (2-5-1), and Indianapolis (2-7) on their schedule. That’s five easy victories to get them to 11 wins. item.title: Russell Wilson names his new Super Bowl favourites after the NFL trade deadline
item.description: Photo by Noam Galai/Getty Images The 2026 NFL trade deadline passed on November 10 and on the back of it, Russell Wilson is swaying towards the Minnesota Vikings being his Super Bowl favourites. The Vikings were 6-1 before they played the Buffalo Bills on Monday but they fell to a 23-6 defeat, with quarterback Carson Wentz managing just 81 passing yards compared to 234 for the Bills’ Josh Allen. Wentz’s low output has been an issue for most of the season so far but Minnesota may have solved their quarterback problem after trading for Kirk Cousins. On the back of Cousins returning to the Vikings, Wilson, when speaking about his favourite for the Super Bowl, said that the Vikings ‘just got a few more wins’ after adding the 38-year-old to their roster. Speaking on ‘Set, Hut!’ , the ex-NFL player said: “Credit to the Minnesota Vikings. And these guys, Minnesota Vikings may be my new favourite, for the Super Bowl and getting coming out of the NFC. You got the 49ers, right? Obviously, those guys have been really good all year, watching the Packers and how they’re starting to heat up in this division and everything else. “But now you look at this division: the Minnesota Vikings, right? They just got a few more wins with Kirk Cousins.” Cousins currently has 2,340 passing yards this season, which is the fifth-most in the league. By comparison, Wentz has just 357 yards and the second-lowest completion rate in the NFL (48.4%). item.title: Exeter's Cummins 'fully deserves' Ireland U21 call-up
item.description: Charlie Cummins' goal ensured a memorable FA Cup win at Huddersfield Town on Saturday [Shutterstock] Exeter City manager Matt Taylor says midfielder Charlie Cummins deserves his call-up to the Republic of Ireland's under-21 side. The 21-year-old has been in impressive form this season, scoring three times including the winner in Exeter's 2-1 FA Cup first-round victory at League One leaders Huddersfield Town on Saturday. Cummins has progressed through Exeter's academy system since moving to St James park in January 2024 from Cobh Ramblers for an undisclosed fee. He has been a mainstay of the side this season having started all 14 of Exeter's League Two fixtures. "It's fully deserved. Not just his performances but the way he's conducted himself and he's playing a man's game in a really serious level of football," Taylor told BBC Radio Devon. "So when he goes to under-21s level with Ireland I hope he continues that and looks like he has done. "His goals recently have been an added bonus, but his performances are going from strength to strength. "He fully deserves it, it's great for his family, fantastic for the football club and the academy again, another young player who's now into that international bracket as well as just being a first-team player." Exeter's young squad hailed after memorable FA Cup win Huddersfield Town 1-2 Exeter City Cummins' call-up for the UEFA European Under-21 Championship play-offs against Finland came as a replacement for an injured player. As such it was only announced on Monday and came after the cut-off for Exeter to get Saturday's game with Cheltenham Town postponed. The Grecians also have Kenya's Vincent Harper and Scotland Under-21 player Ethan Sutherland away on international duty. "Two days earlier then the game gets called off if we want it to," added Taylor. "You don't want any game of football called off, I'm not in that mindset whatsoever. "But you also, selfishly as a manager, want your best players available at all times. "You're torn really, but then the administrators and the people who produce a schedule or work to a schedule say if too many games are called off then there's too much to fit in at the back end of the season. "We've not hit the winter months where games might be called off due to the weather or further cup runs. "I've not got the answers, we just feel a little bit hard done by going into this weekend. "But no excuses from me, no excuses from the team. If one player is not available, like some of our players weren't available last weekend, it's an opportunity to see the strength and depth that we've got." item.description: Mauricio Pochettino's possible/probable/impending move to Manchester United — Michael Carrick is still in charge at the moment! — could see limited changes to the team until January. That might sound wild given United's massive struggles this season, but Pochettino like Carrick favors a 4-2-3-1 and the cupboard is relatively bare at Old Trafford despite the club's annual spending spree. item.description: Texas Longhorns Athletic Director Chris Del Conte looks at a replay during the game against the Mississippi Rebelsin the second half at Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin on Saturday Oct. 24, 2026. (Jay Janner/Austin American-Statesman) The Big 12 needs a new commissioner, but Texas Longhorns athletic director Chris Del Conte insists that it won't be him. item.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
item.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. That’s how basketball works. “That allows me to have more space to be the best Ja I can be,” Morant said. The 36-year-old Holiday, who would be a more natural complement next to Lillard or Morant than they are to each other, made his own case for why the point guard rotation makes sense. “It’s about being a complete basketball player for myself,” he said, “and I think we have a lot of guys like that.” There is a long history of teams talking themselves into superstar additions that make little sense. The Los Angeles Lakers once made a conscious decision to acquire Russell Westbrook and pair him with LeBron James. Nobody made them do that! The talent and star power of a Lillard-Morant backcourt is undeniable. Still, I remain unconvinced that Cronin, with a very hands-on new owner in his ear, made the deal with winning basketball games at the front of mind. Although, admittedly, Cronin’s biggest wins as a GM have been in the trade market. The haul of assets he collected for Lillard, only to get him back two years later, will go down as an all-time great swindle. So, too, will the oft-questioned Avdija trade a year later. Maybe he sees something in a Lillard-Morant pairing that many of us can’t. Morant could return to the All-Star form he had achieved before injuries and off-court issues derailed his ascent . Each player needs the ball in his hands to thrive. If the duo is on the floor together, Avdija is no longer the secondary playmaker, he becomes tertiary. So, you are left to wonder whether the Blazers sold themselves on Morant because of how he can help the current collection of talent or if they simply saw the opportunity to land a 27-year-old All-NBA talent for cheap, regardless of what it meant for the existing roster construction. And if you’re being honest, you probably don’t need to wonder which of the two it is. “We were very focused and we’ll continue to be on … adding to our talent base as much as we can,” Cronin said. That thinking right there may tell you just how far ahead of everyone else the San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder are in the Western Conference. They are positioned to dominate for the next half-decade, if not longer. The only chance any other team has of disrupting that is taking bold risks. But I thought the goal was to go all in on the twilight years of Lillard’s career? “Dame literally just wants to win,” said first-year head coach Micah Nori, whose charge is to sort out arguably the most talented glut of point guard talent in NBA history. “I think that’s the only thing left he really has to (do). Or simply give Portland a potential off-ramp if Lillard is no longer the same player after tearing his Achilles tendon? Morant was without question a low-risk, high-reward addition. He came at the reasonable price of Jerami Grant and Kris Murray. item.title: Who will call plays for Oregon after Mehringer's firing?
item.description: EUGENE — After firing first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer seven games into the 2026 season, Dan Lanning shared Oregon ’s plans for filling his role moving forward at his weekly press conference Monday night. Offensive assistant Jay Johnson will lead offensive playcalling for the Ducks going forward, Lanning said. “He has a lot of experience as a play-caller, was with me in Georgia when we were part of the national championship team,” Lanning said. “Went on to have a lot of success in Colorado and Michigan State. He’s gonna lead the efforts there with the offensive staff, but it’ll still be a collaborative effort, with a lot of the work that we do. “He’s also coming in with a different perspective, a different view, not being with us the last few years, where he can provide a couple things that might be different than what we’ve done.” Mehringer, previously the tight ends coach for the Ducks, is the first assistant coach Lanning has fired in his tenure at Oregon, which began in 2022. item.title: Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'
item.description: EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday. “There was an incident this weekend that didn’t match our standard here in our program,” Lanning said. “There will be an appropriate action taken. Still gathering some details with what that situation looks like. But that would be handled internally. I’m not gonna respond to any other questions about that. We’re gonna handle that with our guys. “There’s an expectation of what you have to... how you have to act, and how you need to perform in our program. Kind of overshadows the success that we had on Saturday, which is disappointing, but that will be handled by us internally. I’m not going to speak on it publicly.” When Lanning was asked a follow-up question about a rumored speeding incident involving other Oregon football players, for which there haven’t been any confirmed arrests, he said, “I was talking about the same thing when I first addressed it.” This is also the second instance of an Oregon football team member facing DUII charges in the past year. In April, running backs coach Ra’Shaad Samples allegedly backed his Ford F-150 into a parked car outside a bar in Eugene. His next court date is Oct. 27. An arraignment for Stewart in his DUII case hasn’t been set, as official charges haven’t been filed to Springfield Municipal Court as of Monday evening, according to court records. Ezenwata hit the post, whilst Williams-Barnett was left embarrassed as his chipped effort was saved. Though Slovenia did get on the scoresheet, Salmon will be pleased to have debuted in a comfortable victory, as he played the full 90 minutes of the match. The Belarus game is on November 14th at 12:00 GMT, and the Austria match is on November 17th at 13:00 GMT. Now in year three, how has the guard improved her game and how far can she take the Buckeyes? Name: Jaloni Cambridge Position: Guard Class: Junior High School: Montverde Academy H.S. (Montverde, Florida) 2025-26 Stats: 23.2 ppg, 5.6 rpg, 4.4 apg, 49.4 FG%, 36.0 3PT FG%, 82.4 FT% Last Season Cambridge entered the 25-26 with team leadership firmly in her hands. The point guard’s freshman season was a crash course of learning to adjust to the size of college players and learning to play alongside other athletes who were also the big names at their high schools and academies. From the performances Cambridge exhibited last season, it was clear that she was trying to do it all for the Buckeyes. Cambridge led the team in scoring in 26 of 32 games and all but five Big Ten games. In seven matchups, Cambridge scored at least 30 points and twice scored 41 points. Those games were also not against mid-majors in the non-conference schedule. Six of the seven games were against Power Four opponents, which included the Notre Dame Fighting Irish in the NCAA Tournament’s Second Round. The first came against the Illinois Fighting Illini when the point guard completely took over the second half against another young and talented side led by then sophomore Berry Wallace. In front of Cambridge’s favorite WNBA player A’ja Wilson, who sat court side at the game in Champaign, Illinois, Cambridge was unstoppable in the second half. All season, Cambridge showed that the moment was never too big. Against the Michigan Wolverines, down three points with less than one second left, Cambridge got to the foul line and hit all three free throws to get the Buckeyes to overtime, where the Wolverines ultimately capitalized on a rushed final offensive possession by Ohio State. Through the play of Cambridge, the Buckeyes were one of only two Big Ten teams to play within 10 points of the eventual national champions in the UCLA Bruins. Although in the Big Ten Tournament against the Bruins, Cambridge was caught doing too much for the Buckeyes and head coach Cori Close was ready through center Lauren Betts. The 6-foot-7 center who won the Big Ten Defensive Player of the Year was on Cambridge when she went inside and made the game difficult for the then sophomore. Even so, the success of a fourth place finish in a competitive Big Ten conference for a team full of underclassmen points back to the play of Cambridge. The point guard ended the season atop the Big Ten scoring numbers with 813 points and 23.2 points per game. It earned her spots on the Coaches and Media First Team All-Big Ten and an Associated Press Second Team All-American honor. What to Expect A better question for Cambridge is what not to expect from the dynamic junior. At 5’7, she can’t dunk. That’s about it. Cambridge is still a three-level scorer, she is still fast and she still plays strong on the defensive end of the court. What will be different is the guard’s strength overall. In the offseason, the guard said she spent more time in the gym lifting weights than she did on the basketball court, which means a lot considering the work she puts in on the practice court. “I really made an emphasis to get stronger this year, and it’ll definitely show on my body,” Cambridge told reporters. “I felt great, and the results from just like with our strength coach Claire [Quebedeaux]. I mean, you should really see my numbers from last year to this year. I feel faster. I feel so much better than I did last year, and I’m healthier now. So with my Achilles and everything, everything feels good.” The guard’s offensive focuses are on deep shooting and assists. Cambridge was not satisfied with her 3.9 attempted three-point shots per game and 36.0% of her attempts. That has already bumped up after only three games of the 26-27 regular season. Cambridge attempted 5.7 shots from deep and hit 2.0 per game. Against the Central Michigan University Chippewas, Cambridge showed she is still fine with taking over a game sometimes. Cambridge she scored 15 points in the first quarter on 4-of-5 shooting and she still added in four assists. Also expect a jump in leadership ability. Ohio State was young last year and it was a crash course for the then sophomore point guard. In year three, the poise of being a leader and running the game on and off the court shows in Cambridge, but granted it came against sides where the Scarlet and Gray did not face a lot of adversity. Prediction It is hard to imagine Jaloni Cambridge being better, but in year two of being a formal leader on the roster, she will impact games even more. There will still be blistering runs to the basket but Cambridge’s game will be smarter. The point guard won’t force her game inside but instead force opponents to adjust to her adjustments. If the team around Cambridge stays healthy, the offensive load will not solely be atop her shoulders, like it was last season. The two key areas to watch in Cambridge’s growth will be how she gets those teammates involved in games. It is still far too early to say its worked but the guard’s assists are up from 4.4 last season to 6.0 per game in the 26-27 season. Also, the guard’s scoring is down, but Cambridge will tell anyone who asks that a win with her scoring less points is better than a loss with her atop the stat sheet in the points column. An added source of motivation for Cambridge is playing her last season alongside sister Kennedy Cambridge. Now, Jaloni Cambridge does not need much in the motivation department but the two said their goal is to get to at least the Sweet Sixteen. There is also a pair of big games in Columbus in March when Nationwide Arena hosts the Final Four a few miles away from the Ohio State campus. Jaloni Cambridge has the ability to lead the program to new heights, but she won’t be able to do it alone. Two laps later Antonelli went off in Turn 1 as his car's rear end suddenly snapped under braking, spitting Antonelli out into the run-off area. The Italian recovered but lost the lead to Norris and dropped further down the order to finish fifth, 41 seconds behind Norris. item.description: Credit: OutKick, Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Craig Carton knows a thing or two about the perils of gambling, and he’s not happy about Dianna Russini’s alignment with online gambling company BetUS. Russini is making her long-awaited return to the sports media world on Wednesday with the debut of a weekly live show for BetUS . It’s a curious landing spot for the former ESPN and The Athletic NFL insider . Her reporting career came crashing down earlier this year following allegations of an intimate relationship with NFL head coach Mike Vrabel, but it was always assumed she’d resurface. Even then, it was presumed that if a mainstream media outlet didn’t want to take a chance on her, one of the major sports betting platforms or prediction markets would add her to their list of sports-centric hosts they’ve been throwing money at. For whatever reason, Russini ended up working with the lesser-known BetUS, for whom The Russini Report will be its most high-profile show by a mile. Carton, whose own sports media career was rocked by scandal, knows quite a bit about the sports betting world. His initial stint with WFAN ended when a gambling addiction led to his arrest for securities and wire fraud. He eventually found his way back to WFAN (for a third time) with The Carton Show with Craig Carton & Chris McMonigle , and he’s spent a lot of time speaking out about the dangers of gambling addiction and the many ways the industry takes advantage of people. item.title: Former top recruit among Commodores to know vs. Vanderbilt in Week 11
item.description: The Vanderbilt Commodores have certainly given the Alabama Crimson Tide problems each of the last two seasons. Led by quarterback Diego Pavia, Vanderbilt stunned the Crimson Tide in Nashville during the 2024 season, 40-35, a result which snapped a lengthy losing streak in the series. Vanderbilt then gave the Tide problems once again a year ago in Tuscaloosa as well, with Alabama eventually pulling away in the second half to avenge that 2024 loss, 30-14. This season, Vanderbilt will face the Crimson Tide with a 4-5 (1-5 SEC) record that has seen the Commodores drop five of their last six games. The Commodores are still led by head coach Clark Lea, and sport a roster that features a number of players who have faced Alabama before, as well as some who have not, in key positions. Here are five Vanderbilt Commodores to know ahead of Week 11 , as well as how each has performed before against the Tide. Jared Curtis, Quarterback Vanderbilt's starting quarterback is Jared Curtis, a true freshman who has completed 64.7% of his passes for 1,657 yards and an 8:8 TD:INT ratio over eight games this season. A top recruit in the 2026 high school class, Curtis also has 76 rushes for 172 yards and two touchdowns this season, and is set to face Alabama for the first time. Junior Sherrill, Wide Receiver Junior Sherrill is undoubtedly Vanderbilt's top pass catching option who currently leads the Commodores with 747 yards and four touchdowns this season on 56 receptions. The senior wideout is also averaging 23.8 yards over six kick returns this season, and is set to face Alabama for the third time. Sherrill has a combined eight receptions for 94 yards and a touchdown against the Tide over the last two seasons. CJ Heard, Safety CJ Heard is leading the Vanderbilt defense with 64 total tackles this season, 44 of which have been solo, while also having recorded four TFL, three sacks, one interception, six pass defenses, and two forced fumbles. The junior had eight tackles, six of which were solo, against the Crimson Tide a year ago. Sedrick Alexander, Running Back The Commodores' leading rusher is Sedrick Alexander with 333 yards and six touchdowns on 85 carries, while the senior also has 17 receptions for 153 yards and another score this season. Over the last two years, Alexander has rushed for a combined 140 yards and three touchdowns on 25 attempts against Alabama. The running back also had five receptions for 46 yards and another touchdown as a receiver. Nick Rinaldi, Linebacker Nick Rinaldi is another name on the Vanderbilt defense enjoying a solid season with 58 total tackles, 29 of which have been solo, as well as 5.5 TFL, 3.5 sacks, and five pass defenses. The graduate student linebacker has five tackles, one TFL, one sack, and a pass defense in two career games against Alabama. item.description: Plus: more speedy marathons by footballers, headed goals of the season and chairs acting as managers Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Which club team has had the most international captains playing together at one time?” asks MH Zahid. “Conversely, which international team has had the most club captains in its starting lineup at one time?” A quick web search finds a fuss being made in various corners of the internet of Chelsea’s 2009-10 squad because it contained six national team captains in Michael Ballack (Germany), Petr Cech (Czech Republic), Didier Drogba (Côte d’Ivoire), Branislav Ivanovic (Serbia), Mikel John Obi (Nigeria) and John Terry (England). These are, indeed, six people who captained their countries, playing together at one time, but crucially they were not all international captains at that time, which because we like to have our hands bound as tight as possible – no questions please – mean they are disqualified from this particular tournament. Ivanovic, you see, was not named Serbia captain until 2012 and Mikel, who was but a whippersnapper at 22 when the 2009-10 season started, was still seven years from getting his hands on the Nigeria armband. item.title: From W-M to the No 10, shirt numbers tell a story of football’s tactical evolution
item.description: In the days before squad numbers, the number on a shirt was an indicator of position, as well as the attributes a player was supposed to demonstrate Ultimate 1-50: check out our complete list of players Numbers have a fascination. The No 10 is revered almost everywhere, but perhaps most especially in Argentina, where it denotes the playmaker, the enganche , the quasi-mythical figure who links the front and back of the team. Liverpool and Manchester United have reasons to celebrate their No 7. Ajax retired No 14 for Johan Cruyff, Milan their No 3 and No 6 for Paolo Maldini and Franco Baresi respectively and Birmingham their 22 for Jude Bellingham as gestures of respect for their abilities. Other numbers have been retired to mark premature deaths: the No 20 at Liverpool for Diogo Jota, the No 23 at Manchester City for Marc-Vivian Foé, the 21 at Espanyol for Daniel Jarque. But numbers are not just about individuals. In the days before squad numbers, the number on a shirt was an indicator of position, and the expectations of particular numbers in particular cultures, as well as the attributes a player in that shirt was supposed to demonstrate, themselves tell a story of tactical evolution. item.title: Football Daily | Manchester United, Aston Villa and the unseriousness of a 4-4 draw
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Precisely 13,266 games have been played since the inception of the Premier League, and 19 of those matches have finished 4-4 (0.1%), a rarity in a division dominated by the mighty 1-0 (17.6%). It was about time we got one, though. The months of August and September, when teams are still fighting to define their top-flight seasons and fitness and motivation tend to be at their peak, have never seen a single 4-4 draw. As motivation decreases the chances of stupid scorelines increase, and that’s where the 4-4 creeps in. There’s a certain on-the-beachness inherent in the score, and it is no coincidence that it has occurred more in the second half of April, as thoughts drift to the close season and the ineffable pointlessness of a lot of late-campaign football becomes unavoidable, than in the entirety of any other month. Students, teachers and visitors at the University of Queensland can view the world’s longest-running experiment. The flamin’ pitch drop experiment began in 1930 and is designed to demonstrate how an apparent solid (pitch) behaves like an extremely viscous liquid. Nearly 100 years ago pitch was placed in a funnel and kept at room temperature. It moves incredibly slowly at a rate of approximately one atom per second (slower than the continental drift), and only nine drips have ever been recorded , though never witnessed. item.title: Manchester City’s weaknesses under Enzo Maresca are being exposed
item.description: After three straight defeats, City’s manager says he will use the international break to reassess. Their problems may go beyond tactics Sign up for our free newsletter here Enzo Maresca seemed, if not quite baffled by his side’s Saturday defeat to Nottingham Forest, then at least a little put out. After seven straight wins from the start of the season, that’s now three straight defeats, a pattern so unusual that it’s been recorded only once before in top-flight English history, by Sheffield Wednesday in 1904-05. The three defeats were all different, Maresca said, although in all of them City had had more possession and more chances. In the 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa two weeks ago, City had 63% of the ball and had 15 chances to Villa’s eight. In the 1-0 home defeat to Brighton last weekend, they had 62% possession and 21 chances to seven. At the City Ground, it was 79% possession and 12 chances to 11. So Maresca is right in one way: City could look at basic statistics and say they had been unfortunate – although Forest could equally point to the fact that they went into that game third top of the expected goals table but second-bottom of the actual table. This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Delap’s talents resurface in style, Gómez delights Brighton with more fireworks, and hair-pulling confusion at Everton It would have been very easy for Oliver Glasner to lose patience with Liam Delap. The forward is still only 23, yet the days when he was rattling in 12 in a Premier League season for Ipswich have come to seem a very long time ago (and his six games for Manchester City even longer). A season at Chelsea had left him bereft of confidence, an odd mix of diffidence and overaggression, devoid of composure in the box, arms flailing like a broken windmill. But the old gifts have not left him. Both goals on Saturday were the result of great muscular surges and if the first finish seemed essentially about hitting the ball as hard as possible on target, the second was a precise – and still powerful – finish in off the far post. After games such as this it’s possible to imagine him as England’s long-term replacement for Harry Kane. item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

item.title: Billions in revenue proves Fifa right on the World Cup – but only on things it cares about
item.description: The 2026 edition of the tournament brought in untold amounts of money to Gianni Infantino’s governing body The total hasn’t entirely stopped rising yet, still clicking away towards a final tally. Still, Fifa has already announced that it surpassed its own lofty revenue projections for the 2026 World Cup, bringing in $15bn, significantly more than anticipated. It appears that a third of that total – $5bn – came from ticket sales and hospitality alone, per reporting from the Times . That would mean direct income from the matchgoing fans came in five times as high in the United States, Canada and Mexico as it did at the last World Cup, in Qatar in 2022, when the total stood at $929m. While 2026’s expanded World Cup added 40 games to the schedule, the takings nevertheless went from an average of about $14.5m per match to about $48m. Continue reading...

item.title: Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or party gives way to anxiety-filled hangover for Bayern Munich | Andy Brassell
item.description: Dortmund did not read the script, remaining level on points with the defending champions at the top of the table It was the moment they had all been … not so much waiting for, but planning, pushing and yearning for. In the videos that announce the starting lineup on the giant scoreboard before kick-off, every Bayern Munich player turns to face the camera with their personal salute, greeting or goal celebration, the playful progression from the standard folding of arms. Except on Saturday evening, the No 9 turned around smiling, and cradling the golden trophy. In the midweek DFB Pokal stroll against Magdeburg there had been a salute, the players welcoming Harry Kane on to the pitch with a guard of honour to commemorate his Ballon d’Or victory two nights before. This, however, was the real party, the moment where the England captain’s and Bayern’s successful union and the apex it has reached was celebrated in front of a global audience. There was every reason to believe it would be a full and satisfying victory lap, even in Der Klassiker, with proper competition so often bringing the best out of the Rekordmeister. item.title: Folarin Balogun takes a first, tiny step toward moving on from a calamitous summer
item.description: The USMNT striker scored his first goal since the World Cup in a losing effort against Paris FC. Could it lead to something more? Before this weekend, the last time Folarin Balogun scored was in the United States’ 2-0 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina at this past summer’s World Cup. In the immediate aftermath, the outlook for Balogun seemed rosy; an ascendant player who could muster a goal in tense games. At half-time against Bosnia, US fans weren’t just wondering how far his team could advance – they were sizing Balogun up against some of the world’s best strikers. But for most of the ensuing four months, Balogun has been in limbo. His breakout World Cup was overshadowed by a red card in that same game against Bosnia and Herzegovina, followed by a scandal of which he wanted no part. Just as it seemed a summer move away from Monaco could get his club career on track, he broke off a possible deadline-day move to Everton after a lengthy visit to the training grounds and a medical he felt was improperly handled. item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
